statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(nums) - L, where L is the maximum k for which there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(nums) with k >= 3 and some p, 0 < p < k-1, such that nums[j_0] < ... < nums[j_p] > ... > nums[j_{k-1}]. Such a sequence nums[j_0],...,nums[j_{k-1}] is called a mountain subsequence of nums.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; and there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(nums) with k >= 3 and some p, 0 < p < k-1, such that nums[j_0] < ... < nums[j_p] > ... > nums[j_{k-1}].

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(nums) with k = len(nums) - r, k >= 3, and some p, 0 < p < k-1, such that nums[j_0] < ... < nums[j_p] > ... > nums[j_{k-1}]. In other words, nums has a mountain subsequence of length len(nums)-r.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if nums itself is a mountain array, i.e., len(nums) >= 3 and there exists p with 0 < p < len(nums)-1 such that nums[0] < nums[1] < ... < nums[p] > nums[p+1] > ... > nums[len(nums)-1].

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exists an index p with 0 < p < len(nums)-1 for which the following holds. Let incEnd(p) be the maximum length of a strictly increasing subsequence of nums[0..p] that ends at index p (i.e., whose last element is nums[p]), and let decStart(p) be the maximum length of a strictly decreasing subsequence of nums[p..len(nums)-1] that starts at index p (i.e., whose first element is nums[p]). Then incEnd(p) >= 2, decStart(p) >= 2, and incEnd(p) + decStart(p) - 1 = len(nums) - r.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; and there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(nums) with k >= 3 and some p, 0 < p < k-1, such that nums[j_0] < ... < nums[j_p] > ... > nums[j_{k-1}].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(nums) - M, where M is the maximum, over all indices i with 0 < i < len(nums)-1 and with incEnd(i) >= 2 and decStart(i) >= 2, of incEnd(i) + decStart(i) - 1. Here incEnd(i) is the maximum length of a strictly increasing subsequence of nums[0..i] whose last index is i, and decStart(i) is the maximum length of a strictly decreasing subsequence of nums[i..len(nums)-1] whose first index is i. The maximum is taken over a nonempty set by the preconditions.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; and there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(nums) with k >= 3 and some p, 0 < p < k-1, such that nums[j_0] < ... < nums[j_p] > ... > nums[j_{k-1}].

statement: If the function returns r on nums and r' on nums', then r = r'.
preconditions: Take any two slices nums and nums' of the same length such that both satisfy the common preconditions: 3 <= len <= 1000; every value is between 1 and 10^9; and each has a mountain subsequence of length at least 3. Also assume there exists a strictly increasing function f from integers to integers such that nums'[i] = f(nums[i]) for every 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns r on nums, the following holds. For every index d with 0 <= d < len(nums) such that there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(nums) with k = len(nums)-r, k >= 3, none of the j_t equals d, and some p, 0 < p < k-1, satisfying nums[j_0] < ... < nums[j_p] > ... > nums[j_{k-1}], let nums' be the slice obtained from nums by deleting the element at index d.
